name: Midland Terminal Railway station, Cripple Creek (front)
basis: Catalogue record of the holding library, read on 2026-11-24.
notes: Library: 'Front view of Midland Terminal Railway station, constructed in 1896 ... the two-story brick building has a stone foundation and/or basement ... billboard on footbridge reads "Owl Cigars"'. Title supplied by the cataloguer. Looked at before use: the whole face of the depot square-on: rock-faced stone ground storey with round-arched openings, brick upper storeys, a gabled porch in the middle over a sign 'MIDLAND TERMINAL', and at the right a timber stair up to the footbridge with an Owl Cigars billboard. Scratches and a worn corner on the negative; no caption or mark on the copy.

name: Midland Terminal Railway station, Bennett Avenue, Cripple Creek
basis: Catalogue record of the holding library, read on 2026-11-24.
notes: Library: 'Crowd gathers near Midland Terminal Railway Station constructed in 1896, Bennett Avenue ... miners with lunch buckets, horse-drawn carriage ... "Assay Office" lettered on window; "Midland Terminal" sign is on a second-story porch.' Title supplied by the cataloguer. Looked at before use: looking along Bennett Avenue to the depot standing across its end, with brick business blocks on the left, a crowd of men with lunch pails and a horse and buggy. This is the depot standing in the line of the avenue, as both Sanborn sheets draw it. No caption or mark on the copy.

name: Union Depot sign on the Midland Terminal station, Cripple Creek
basis: Catalogue record of the holding library, read on 2026-11-24.
notes: Library: 'Close-up view of station names ... "M. T. Ry. - C. S. C. C. D., Union Depot" and "Postal Telegraph Co., Branch Office - Up Stairs."' Title supplied by the cataloguer. Looked at before use: the middle bay of the depot from below: the sign under the porch reads 'C S & C C D and M T Ry UNION DEPOT' (the 'and' small, between the lines), a Postal Telegraph-Cable Co. sign over a stone arch, and at the right the timber trestle of the footbridge. No mark on the copy. The sign shows the Short Line shared the depot at the date of the photograph, which is not known closer than the library's range.

name: Cripple Creek, with a Short Line train at the Midland Terminal depot
basis: Catalogue record of the holding library, read on 2026-11-24.
notes: Library: 'View of a Colorado Springs & Cripple Creek District Railway train at the Midland Terminal Railway depot'; typed on the envelope: 'View of Cripple Creek, Colo. showing CS & CCD train at left.' H. E. High; copy glass negative, from R. H. Kindig. Looked at before use: the town from a grassy rise, with an engine and coach on a trestle at the left, a yard of flat cars in a cut, another long trestle at the right with a box car lettered 'Colorado ...' below it, and the street grid rising to the hills behind. The depot is not picked out at this size. No mark on the copy.

name: Midland Terminal 'Y', Cripple Creek
basis: Catalogue record of the holding library, read on 2026-11-24.
notes: Library: 'View of Midland Terminal Railway wye, Poverty Gulch ... engine with passenger cars crosses trestle ... two men stand on center of wye near Bob Womack's original prospect site ... dump carts used by railroad in construction of wye'. Title hand-lettered on the original negative; on the back of the cabinet card: 'Cripple Creek, Railroad yards, probably before 1900, the Y - Midland Terminal'. Looked at before use: a train backing round a curved timber trestle in snow, a second long trestle across the gulch behind, dump carts and timbers in the foreground, cabins on the hillsides. The photographer's title is lettered along the bottom edge of the negative: the maker's own, so nothing needs cropping. The wye has not been located.

name: Cripple Creek (W. H. Jackson, 1897)
basis: Catalogue record of the holding library, read on 2026-11-24.
notes: Library: 'Shows residential outbuildings, Portland Hotel, and trestle for the Midland Terminal Railway.' Attributed to Jackson from a bound sample album; 'Hand-lettered title and "Copyright" reproduced in print'; number 4277 on the negative. Looked at before use: the town from a bare slope with sheds in the foreground, brick blocks in the middle and the hillside streets beyond. '4277 COPYRIGHT 1897' is lettered on the negative (the maker's). There is also a faint pencilled 'Cripple Creek' on the bottom margin of the print, someone else's note; it is on the mount edge, outside the picture. Stains in the sky. The trestle was not picked out.

name: Florence and Cripple Creek Railroad station, Cripple Creek
basis: Catalogue record of the holding library, read on 2026-11-24.
notes: Library: 'the two-story wooden frame multi-gabled building ... signs on depot include: "Cripple Creek," "F. & C. C. Suburban Train Schedule from Victor to Goldfield," and banner with: "Basket Picnic, $1.50, Canon City and Return ..."'. Title supplied by the cataloguer. Looked at before use: the frame station from across the tracks: a long one-storey building with a two-storey gabled middle, a bay window, a bracketed shed roof at the right end, a 'CRIPPLE CREEK' board, the picnic banner and a timetable board; hillside houses behind. Cracks and scratches in the negative; no caption or mark on the copy. The form fits the 1900 Sanborn sheet's depot, one storey with a two-storey middle.

name: Cripple Creek depot, F. & C. C. R. R. (halftone of 1896)
basis: Catalogue record of the holding library, read on 2026-11-24.
notes: Library: 'Title from printed label on original halftone; photograph of a photograph originally reproduced in "Cripple Creek and Colorado Springs Illustrated" printed in 1896.' The library dates its copy 1960-1970. Looked at before use: the same frame station from the other end, with a narrow-gauge engine and train at the left, a horse and buggy and baggage carts at the platform, rock in the foreground; the halftone screen shows. No caption on the copy. The picture itself was published in 1896 (by the library's note), so it is shown as a library copy of a pre-1931 picture.

name: Last Midland Terminal passenger train, Cripple Creek
basis: Catalogue record of the holding library, read on 2026-11-24.
notes: Library: 'last run of February 6, 1949 ... train warms up its engines at the Midland Terminal station; side rear view of depot constructed in 1896 ... round tower with bay windows'. Title, date and photographer written on the back of the print. Looked at before use: people in winter coats walking along the snowy track towards the rear of a train standing beside the depot, whose round tower with its conical roof is the bay the Sanborn sheets draw on the east side; rock cutting on both sides. No mark on the copy.

name: The Old Depot, Cripple Creek (postcard)
basis: Catalogue record of the holding library, read on 2026-11-24.
notes: Library: 'Cripple Creek station of the Midland Terminal Railway, now the Cripple Creek District Museum. Printed on back "The Old Depot/Cripple Creek, Colo."' John F. McClenahan Postcard Collection. Looked at before use: a real-photo postcard of the depot's face, square-on, with 'THE OLD DEPOT' and 'CRIPPLE CREEK, COLO.' lettered in white across the bottom (the publisher's own). No museum sign, no footbridge, a stair up the cutting at the right. Undated; its title, 'the old depot', and the missing footbridge suggest after the railway closed in 1949. That is a reading, not a date, so it is treated as after 1930.
